contribution: Combines behaviour trees, reinforcement learning and control barrier functions so learned subtask controllers avoid undoing earlier subtasks, cutting action-condition violations from 8.8 to 1.4 percent against a reward-penalty baseline.
flag: SINGLE-AGENT: one point-mass agent in Unity; multi-agent RL appears only in related work, so the maintainer may well prefer exclude-E4. Retained because the CBF action mask is a genuine inference-time filter (criterion a) and the behaviour-tree sequence gives a sequential, irreversibility-flavoured safety property - the constraints exist to stop the agent undoing already-achieved subtasks, and the residual 1.4 percent of violations occur at controller handovers.

title: VISTA: A Vision and Intent-Aware Social Attention Framework for Multi-Agent Trajectory Prediction
evidence: Abstract: "a social-token attention module enabling fine-grained interaction modeling across agents" and "pairwise attention maps to show social influence patterns during inference"; "On MADRAS, our approach reduces the average collision rate of strong baselines from 2.14% to 0.03%, and on SDD, it achieves a 0% collision rate".
method: Recursive goal-conditioned transformer: cross-attention fuses a goal-heatmap embedding with past trajectories, social-token self-attention mixes agents at every step, and trajectories are decoded recursively for all agents jointly.
evaluation: MADRAS (nine dense crowd scenes) and SDD; ten-plus baselines including MART; ADE/FDE, minADE/minFDE, AUC and inter-agent collision rate (2.14% to 0.03%, 0% on SDD); component ablations; TITAN RTX.
contribution: A goal-conditioned social-attention transformer for joint pedestrian forecasting cuts predicted inter-agent collision rate to 0.03% in dense crowds while improving displacement error over ten baselines.
flag: Qualifies on (b) only; fails the (c) primacy test because nothing acts on the predictions, so collision rate measures realism of joint forecasts rather than hazards averted. No latency, edge or deferral content; threshold for a collision is dataset-calibrated rather than physical.

title: Virtual Omnidirectional Perception for Downwash Prediction within a Team of Nano Multirotors Flying in Close Proximity
evidence: Abstract: 'our proposed spinning camera is capable of predicting the presence of aerodynamic downwash with an F1 score of over 80 % in a challenging swapping task'; downwash is defined by the inter-robot ellipsoid safety condition (2) in Sec. III-B.
method: Spins a single lightweight monocular camera using the multirotor yaw degree of freedom for virtual omnidirectional neighbour detection, then predicts downwash from learned relative positions.
evaluation: 50k synthetic and ~9k real nano-quadrotor images; Locanet versus Yolo across four yaw rates and three tilts with ground-truth bound; downwash F1, success rate, position error.
contribution: Shows an upward-tilted spinning monocular camera on a 42 g multirotor predicts inter-robot aerodynamic downwash hazards with F1 above 80%, enabling cheap omnidirectional swarm awareness.
flag: Learned hazard detector only: no override or avoidance action (authors list collision avoidance as future work), and inference is off-board (images streamed at ~6 fps over Wi-Fi), so (d) and edge deployment are not supported.

title: Vision-Based Collision Avoidance for Multi-Agent Systems With Intermittent Measurements
evidence: Abstract: "Once a collision is detected, the agents replan their trajectories to follow a circular path centered at the point of collision"; Sec. VI, with the coordination law disabled, "results in a violation of the minimum safety distance requirements, shown in Fig. 5(c)".
method: Decentralised communication-free collision avoidance: on detecting a predicted collision agents switch to a circular detour, and a bearing-only feedback law holds a prescribed phase shift; Lyapunov bounds under a switching sensing digraph.
evaluation: 12-vehicle Simulink/Dubins simulation plus 4-Crazyflie flights; ablation with the coordination law off; metrics inter-agent distance vs dsafe (4.75 m / 0.75 m) and phase-shift error; intermittent sensing via directed topology; no latency figures.
contribution: Decentralised bearing-only collision avoidance replans agents onto a shared circular detour and holds a phase shift, with Lyapunov performance bounds and Crazyflie validation under intermittent sensing.
flag: (a) borderline: the override is a detour replan triggered by collision detection, not a per-command filter. Safety evidence is distance and phase-error traces with an algorithm-off ablation rather than a violation rate. Handles one collision event at a time - cascading encounters and measurement noise are explicitly out of scope (Sec. VIII). Extends the authors' earlier conference version [17].

title: When Not to Write Memory: Governing False Promotion from Correlated Agent Traces
evidence: Abstract: GovMem "estimates dependency-aware support, retrieves counterevidence, assigns scope, and outputs one of three decisions: promote, reject, or needs-review" and "reduces false promotion from 0.597 to 0.040 in the default setting while preserving 0.960 recall, at an explicit review burden."
method: Side-agent write-path gate for agent memory: clusters candidate claims, estimates dependency-aware (non-independent) support across agent traces, retrieves counterevidence, assigns scope, then promotes, rejects or routes to human review.
evaluation: Synthetic GovMem-Bench, 120 human-labelled real-trace candidates, 133 adjudicated external candidates; baselines raw frequency, source+scope, confidence scoring, GPT-5.5 judge, GovMem-lite; false promotion, recall, review burden, AUPRC.
gap_cells: multi-agent state; non-generative inference; human handoff
contribution: Treats agent memory writes as evidence governance: a dependency-aware gate promotes, rejects or defers candidate memories, cutting false promotion from correlated multi-agent traces at a measured review cost.
flag: Authors themselves frame it as "a diagnostic governance design point, not as a generally validated or efficient automatic memory writer": held-out false promotion stays at 0.111, review burden 0.692, direct recall 0.448, and final human adjudication rejected all 133 external automatic-promotion candidates including all 11 verification-gate positives. Logical/software domain only; no latency or cost measurement.

title: hGCBF: Heterogeneous Graph Control Barrier Functions for Safe Multi-Agent Systems
evidence: Sec. III-A: 'A safe control input is then synthesized by solving the following QP, which minimizes the deviation from the nominal controller while satisfying the hGCBF safety constraint'; Sec. IV-A benchmarks the method 'against the following safety filters: 1) DCBF ... 2) GCBF+'.
method: Learned graph control barrier function for heterogeneous MAS: zero-padding unifies state/action spaces; heterogeneous GNN with type embeddings and decoupled attention jointly learns certificate and distributed controller distilled from QP filter.
evaluation: 2D/3D simulation, 128-512 agents, 32 episodes x 3 seeds; baselines DCBF and GCBF+; safety/success rate (86.23% vs 58.8% at N=512), constraint-violation rates, four-variant ablation; no latency or hardware.
contribution: First neural control barrier function for heterogeneous multi-agent systems, using a type-aware graph network to certify and filter nominal control, holding 86% safety at 512 agents where homogeneous baselines collapse.
flag: Deployed controller is a GNN distillation of the centralized QP filter, so the runtime veto is learned rather than solved online; purely simulated, no latency or hardware numbers (DCBF only 'fails completely at N=512 due to substantial computational overhead'); 2D and 3D are both physical sims, so no cross-domain cell.
